'''Amin Shokrollahi''' (born 1964) is a German-Iranian mathematician who has worked on a variety of topics including [[coding theory]] and algebraic [[Computational complexity theory|complexity theory]]. He is best known for his work on iterative decoding of graph based [[forward error correction code|code]]s for which he received the IEEE Information Theory Paper Award of 2002 (together with [[Michael Luby]], [[Michael Mitzenmacher]], and [[Daniel Spielman]], as well as Tom Richardson and Ruediger Urbanke).<ref>{{cite web|title=Information Theory Paper Award|publisher=[[IEEE Information Theory Society]]|url=http://www.itsoc.org/honors/information-theory-paper-award|access-date=May 20, 2012}}</ref> He is one of the inventors of a modern class of practical [[erasure code]]s known as [[tornado code]]s,<ref>{{cite book
|author=Michael G. Luby
|author2=Michael Mitzenmacher
|author3=M. Amin Shokrollahi
|author4=Daniel A. Spielman
|author5=Volker Stemann
|title=Proceedings of the twenty-ninth annual ACM symposium on Theory of computing - STOC '97
|chapter=Practical loss-resilient codes
|chapter-url=http://portal.acm.org/citation.cfm?id=258573
|publisher=ACM
|pages=150–159
|year=1997|doi=10.1145/258533.258573
|isbn=978-0897918886
|s2cid=8625981
}}</ref>
and the principal developer of [[raptor code]]s,<ref>{{cite journal
|author=Amin Shokrollahi
|title=Raptor Codes
|journal=IEEE Transactions on Information Theory
|volume=52
|issue=6
|pages=2551–2567
|year=2006|doi=10.1109/TIT.2006.874390
|s2cid=61814971
}}</ref>
which belong to a class of rateless erasure codes known as [[Fountain code]]s. In connection with the work on these codes, he received the [[IEEE Eric E. Sumner Award]] in 2007 together with Michael Luby "for bridging mathematics, Internet design and mobile broadcasting as well as successful standardization"<ref>{{cite web
|title=IEEE Eric E. Sumner Award Recipients
|url=http://www.ieee.org/about/awards/bios/sumner_recipients.html
|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130112210801/http://www.ieee.org/about/awards/bios/sumner_recipients.html
|url-status=dead
|archive-date=January 12, 2013
|publisher=[[IEEE]]
|access-date={{Format date|2011|2|27}}
}}</ref> and the [[IEEE Richard W. Hamming Medal]] in 2012 together with Michael Luby "for the conception, development, and analysis of practical rateless codes".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ieee.org/documents/hamming_rl.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100620000223/http://ieee.org/documents/hamming_rl.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 20, 2010 |title=IEEE Richard W. Hamming Medal Recipients |publisher=IEEE |access-date={{Format date|2011|1|5}}}}</ref> He also received the 2007 joint Communication Society and Information Theory Society best paper award <ref>{{cite web|title=IEEE Communications Society & Information Theory Society Joint Paper Award|publisher=[[IEEE Communications Society]]|url=http://www.comsoc.org/about/memberprograms/comsoc-awards/joint|access-date=May 20, 2012}}</ref> as well as the 2017 [[Mustafa Prize]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Laureates of 2017|publisher=[[Mustafa Awards Foundation]]|url=http://mustafaprize.org/page/?id=21|access-date=Dec 7, 2017}}</ref> for his work on raptor codes.

He is the principal inventor of Chordal Codes, a new class of codes specifically designed for communication on electrical wires between chips. In 2011 he founded the company [[Kandou Bus]] dedicated to commercialization of the concept of Chordal Codes. The first implementation, transmitting data on 8 correlated wires and implemented in a 40&nbsp;nm process, received the Jan Van Vessem Award for best European Paper at the [[International Solid-State Circuits Conference]] (ISSCC) 2014.
